excerpt: Velo turns screen recordings, docs and prompts into narrated product demos, training and support videos. Free plan; Pro $49/month.
content:
Velo is an AI video tool for companies. You record your screen, paste a URL, upload a deck or type a prompt, and Velo writes the script, adds narration and builds a finished video. It can also turn existing material such as help-centre articles, SOPs, changelogs and call notes into videos, and update a video when the product or process changes instead of making you record it again. Typical uses are product demos, sales videos, customer onboarding and support, and employee training.

Other features listed on the site include an agentic screen recorder, an AI editor, voice cloning, avatars, a brand kit, translation into more than 25 languages, viewer analytics, MCP support and SCORM export for learning systems. The Enterprise plan adds SSO, SAML, SCIM, data residency and API access, and the site states SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance.

Velo is operated by Flowframe, Inc., with a contact address in Delaware, USA. Its About page names Sourav Sanyal and Ajay Kumar as founders and says they have worked together since 2018 on AI for cameras, video infrastructure and computer vision. There is a free plan with 1,500 credits a month; Pro costs $49 a month. On Product Hunt the product has 2 reviews averaging 4.5 out of 5.

Velo launched on Product Hunt on 15 July 2026 and finished #2 for the day, with 570 upvotes and 147 comments. It has 2 Product Hunt reviews averaging 4.5 out of 5 (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Velo ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing page, About page, terms and privacy policy, its Product Hunt listing and the official pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.summary_short: Turns screen recordings, docs and prompts into narrated demo, training and support videos
use_cases: Turning a rough screen recording into a narrated product demo
Making onboarding and support videos from help-centre articles
Turning SOPs and compliance documents into training videos
Updating demo videos after a product change without re-recording
Translating videos into more than 25 languages

fit: make product demos, how-to or training videos regularly and dislike re-recording
run support, onboarding or L&D and already have the material in docs or a help centre
need enterprise controls such as SSO, SCORM export or data residency
not_fit: want a general-purpose creative video editor: Velo is built around work and product videos
need refunds on unused time: the terms say fees are generally non-refundable
only record the occasional quick video message, where a free recorder may be enough

pricing.intro: Prices are from Velo's own pricing page, shown with a $ sign. Usage is measured in credits; the page's estimator assumes about 150 credits per minute of video.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 1,500 credits a month, roughly 2 to 5 minutes of video

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: 3,000 credits a month, roughly 5 to 10 minutes of video; for one person making demos and explainers weekly

plans.name: Ultra
plans.detail: 30,000 credits a month, roughly 50 to 100 minutes of video; more voices, avatars and shared team workflows

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: SSO, SAML, SCIM, RBAC, data residency, SCORM export, API and SDK access, custom voices and avatars, SLA

notes: Yearly billing is cheaper; see the pricing page for the yearly rates.
Add-ons such as premium voices, custom backgrounds and translation use extra credits.
Paid plans renew automatically; the terms say fees are generally non-refundable except where the law requires or after certain system glitches.

alternatives.intro: Other tools that turn recordings or text into explainer and training videos. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Synthesia
items.what: AI avatar video platform for training and communications
items.difference: Centred on AI presenters reading a script, rather than on polishing screen recordings into demos.

items.name: guidde
items.what: Turns screen recordings and files into how-to videos and walkthroughs
items.starts_at: Free; Pro $29 per creator a month
items.difference: Closest like-for-like for documentation videos; Velo adds avatars, workflow-triggered videos and auto-updating demos.

items.name: Loom
items.starts_at: Free Starter; Business $18 per user a month
items.difference: Records you as you are; Velo writes and narrates a polished video from the recording.

pros: Builds a narrated video from a recording, URL, deck or prompt
Can update existing videos when the product changes
Translation into 25+ languages and SCORM export for training
Enterprise security options and stated SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance
cons: Free plan covers only a few minutes of video a month
Credit-based pricing makes cost per video harder to predict
Many enterprise features sit behind custom pricing

posts.author: Fakhr
posts.text: A user describes recording a screen once, mistakes included, and having Velo turn the raw recording into a polished video.

faq.a: An AI video tool that turns screen recordings, documents, URLs, decks or prompts into narrated videos for demos, sales, support, onboarding and training.
There is a free plan with 1,500 credits a month, roughly 2 to 5 minutes of video. Pro is $49 a month and Ultra $200 a month; Enterprise is priced on request.

faq.q: How is Velo different from a video editor?
faq.a: Velo says an editor only changes a video after it exists, whereas Velo creates, updates, translates, hosts and shares video from your company's knowledge.

faq.q: Can it update videos when my product changes?
faq.a: Yes. The site lists auto-updating demos, so you do not have to re-record when a product or process changes.
Flowframe, Inc., which operates Velo. Its About page names Sourav Sanyal and Ajay Kumar as founders.
guidde for how-to videos from recordings, Synthesia for AI-avatar videos and Loom for plain screen recording.
